headline: Signal flat (0); still only 7-18 live trades, net negative but sample far too thin to judge; BTC ~$62.6k
regime_note: No live exposure right now (signal=0). This is a marginal mean-reversion fade whose expected gross edge (~4 bps/bet) is dwarfed by trade-to-trade noise, so a dozen-odd losers is well within random variation.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing:** No position on right now (signal=0), BTC ~$62.6k. The live tally is still tiny: the ledger shows **7 resolved trades** averaging **-17.2 bps** each (total -120 bps), and the broader rolling window shows **18 bets, 55.6% win, net -5.98 bps** (gross -2.98 bps at 3 bps assumed cost).

**What changed vs last time:** Essentially nothing structural. One new losing trade (2026-07-31, -60.9 bps) got added, which is an ugly single outlier but exactly the kind of fat-tail loss you expect when sample size is this small. The picture is the same story as before, just one data point heavier.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us:** With only 7-18 trades, these results are **statistically meaningless** for judging edge. The strategy trades ~1-2% of candles, so the sample grows slowly. Note that even the *gross* figures are slightly negative — mildly discouraging — but a single -61 bps trade dominates the mean, and one bad print can't distinguish 'no edge' from 'normal variance.' The edge-search also found **zero survivors** clearing the profitability bar, consistent with this being a marginal-at-best signal.

**Honest bottom line:** This was always flagged as a marginal candidate whose ~4 bps gross edge likely doesn't survive real costs (~3.9 bps breakeven). Live data so far is negative but far too thin to conclude anything. No action warranted; keep collecting. If net stays clearly negative over several dozen trades, that would justify a 'watch' or pause.
